messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Streaming tail latency spike on /v1/stream — p95 -> 1.2s (baseline 220ms), p99 -> 6.3s. Several client connections showing stalled chunks. Paging @oncall for triage.

maria: taking this, joining now. any customer reports?

kevin: none yet in Support, but metrics show increased error budget burn for a few routes.

jordan: looking at proxy/nginx logs — seeing repeated timeouts while proxying to runtime: 
```
2026-03-17T09:02:41Z proxy-11 nginx[1234]: 2026/03/17 09:02:41 [error] 1234#0: *98765 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: , request: \"GET /v1/stream?model=x\", upstream: \"http://10.5.6.7:8080/stream\"
```
jordan: also seeing `proxy_write_timeout` increments and sockets in CLOSE_WAIT piling up on proxy-11.

abby: on the runtime side early signs of client backpressure: slow-consumer-count on streaming metric climbed from ~2 to ~120 over 5m. consumers with window=0.

maria: likely chain: slow consumers -> backlog at runtime -> longer response generation -> proxy buffers fill -> upstream/read timeouts -> client stalls.

maria: quick mitigation plan (3 steps):
1) flip route to additive fallback (disable chunked streaming for affected route id=rt-42) so responses are sent in larger but fewer chunks.
2) scale proxy pool +2 instances and drop proxy-11 (recycle) to free TCP sockets.
3) enable temporary per-connection send-window throttle at edge to reject extremely slow clients (low-risk).

kevin: how do we flip the route? can you post the exact console API call?

maria: console API to set fallback mode: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/routes/rt-42/actions \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"action":"set_streaming_mode","mode":"chunked_disabled"}'
```

maria: scaling proxy (k8s): 
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/proxy --replicas=6 -n infra
```

maria: recycling instance: 
```bash
kubectl delete pod proxy-11 -n infra
```

jordan: applied the route change at 09:05:03Z. scaling started, proxy-11 eviction requested 09:05:12Z.

abby: I bumped the slow-consumer threshold alarm to avoid noisy paging, and started sampling a few consumer sockets for payload ack times.

kevin: CS asked for a short customer-facing note we can send if they reach out. Draft?

maria: "We observed increased tail latency on streaming responses affecting a subset of connections between 09:00–09:12 UTC. We implemented a routing fallback and scaled proxy capacity; users may have experienced delayed chunk updates but no data loss. We're monitoring and will share an RCA if we see recurrence."

kevin: good. please add incident tag severity=sev2, impacted_routes=rt-42, mitigation=route-fallback+proxy-scale

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2, status=mitigating, started=9255009999, runbook=/playbooks/streaming-tail-latency.

oncall: taking handoff at 09:10Z. I'll monitor p95/p99 and socket counts for next 30m. If p99 > 3s or socket CLOSE_WAIT > 200 for longer than 5m, escalate to SRE lead @maria.

maria: ack handoff. continuing monitoring, will collect traces for a deeper postmortem.

abby: fyi captured sample trace ids: [trace: 0af3, trace: 1b7c, trace: 2f90] — saving to incident folder.

jordan: after route flip and proxy recycle p95 dropped to 280ms and p99 ~1.1s at 09:09Z. slow-consumer-count falling back to baseline.

kevin: marking as watchcall. assigning postmortem owner @jordan. please gather kernel/tcp stats and proxy socket lifecycle events.

maria: noted. thanks team — low-churn follow-up: check if a small regression in chunking algo landed yesterday that changes flush frequency.

oncall: will keep looped in and update every 10m for the next 30. 

maria: :thumbsup:"
